boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Toledo-campus spaces documented by Mercy College for studying, support, reflection, wellness, and campus connection.

cards.title: Mercy College Library
cards.subtitle: Sixth Floor, Jefferson Building
cards.notes: Bring a reading list or laptop, then use the physical collection, computers, printing, and study seating during posted library hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus study-and-research base with collections, computers, printing, and places to work.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College identifies its Library as a place to study, print, or hang out, with computers and physical collections; it lists the location as Sixth Floor Jefferson.
cards.access_notes: Listed library hours are Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; the college says hours may vary.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Sixth Floor, Jefferson Building
cards.notes: Choose a collaborative or private work area that fits the task, and use the wired furniture to connect a personal device.
cards.short_summary: A renovated sixth-floor setting built around different study preferences.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College says the sixth-floor renovation includes a Learning Commons with collaborative spaces, private areas, and wired furniture supporting personal devices.
cards.source_title: Mercy College of Ohio Unveils New Library with Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony
cards.access_notes: Located within the renovated sixth floor near classrooms; confirm building access through the College before visiting.

cards.title: Student Success Center
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Madison Building
cards.notes: Schedule an advising or tutoring appointment when you need help planning coursework, strengthening study skills, or setting academic goals.
cards.short_summary: One office linking students to advising, tutoring, counseling, and retention support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Success Center provides academic advising, tutoring, counseling, and retention support and is listed on the first floor of Madison.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; evening appointments are available upon request.

cards.title: Student Center
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Madison Building
cards.notes: Use this first-floor Madison stop to meet a math or science tutor and arrange a face-to-face session for an individual or small group.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor Madison destination associated with in-person academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College lists its Math and Science Tutor at “1st floor Madison/Student Center” and describes face-to-face tutoring for individuals and small groups.
cards.access_notes: Tutoring is appointment-based; use the College scheduling links or contact the Student Success Center.

cards.title: Testing Center
cards.subtitle: M5802, Fifth Floor, Madison Building
cards.notes: Schedule ahead for an accommodated test, make-up exam, placement test, or distance-education proctoring rather than arriving unannounced.
cards.short_summary: A proctored-testing location for several academic testing needs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Testing Center provides proctoring for accommodated tests, make-up exams, placement tests, and distance-education external proctors; it is in M5802.
cards.access_notes: Appointments require 48 hours’ advance notice and a valid ID. Listed hours: Mon–Thu 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; Fri 8 a.m.–noon.

cards.title: Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, main Jefferson entrance
cards.notes: Follow the posted signs from the main Jefferson entrance, and review the College flyer and waiver information before using the facility.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus fitness room with cardio equipment, weights, mats, and locker rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College says its fitness room has treadmills, exercise bikes, free weights, weight machines, mats, and locker rooms on the second floor by the Jefferson entrance.
cards.access_notes: The College directs users to follow posted signs and provides a fitness-center flyer and waiver form.

cards.title: St. Joseph Chapel
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Mercy College
cards.notes: Stop in for quiet reflection, or join the Wednesday-noon prayer service if that form of community gathering suits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor chapel open to all for reflection, prayer, and weekly services.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College says St. Joseph Chapel is on the first floor, open to all, and used for quiet reflection, sharing, prayer, and Wednesday-noon prayer services.
cards.source_title: The Office of Ministry and Mission | Mercy College
cards.access_notes: The College describes the chapel as open to all; weekly prayer services are Wednesdays at noon.

cards.title: Mercy College Food Pantry
cards.subtitle: Mercy College Toledo campus
cards.notes: If groceries would help, visit while the College is open and complete the anonymous QR questionnaire after using the pantry.
cards.short_summary: A no-appointment campus pantry available to Mercy College community members.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College states that its Food Pantry is available to all students, faculty, and staff, requires no appointment, and may be visited whenever the College is open.
cards.access_notes: No appointment is required; the College says individuals may visit anytime the College is open.

cards.title: Multicultural Center
cards.subtitle: Madison 5617, Madison Building
cards.notes: Use this named gathering space to connect around campus programs that center multicultural awareness, respect, and appreciation.
cards.short_summary: A Madison 5617 gathering space for the college community.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College’s catalog identifies the Multicultural Center in Madison 5617 as a welcoming space for students, faculty, and staff to gather, celebrate, and support one another.
cards.source_title: Mercy College of Ohio College Catalog
cards.access_notes: The catalog places the center in Madison 5617; confirm current room access and programming with Student Affairs.

cards.title: Jefferson Lobby
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Jefferson Building
cards.notes: Use the main entrance near the front desk as a clear meet-up point when you are arriving for a scheduled campus event or visit.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor entrance lobby used for campus registration and information tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College event information identifies the Jefferson lobby near the front desk as the main entrance and a registration point; College communications also document information tables there.
cards.source_title: PA Program Interview Day | Mercy College
cards.access_notes: Access depends on College building hours and the purpose of your visit; the front desk is near the main lobby entrance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission places and activities around Toledo for a low-key outing with friends.

cards.title: Browse the Toledo Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 2445 Monroe St, Toledo
cards.notes: Meet in the Green Building lobby, then make a self-guided loop through the galleries currently open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor art stop with free visitor parking.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that general admission and parking are free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Toledo Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during regular museum hours; some galleries are temporarily closed for renovation and special exhibitions may charge.

cards.title: Take a trail loop at Wildwood
cards.subtitle: 5100 W Central Ave, Toledo
cards.notes: Use the official trail map and keep to marked paths while walking through the preserve’s woods, prairie, and river corridor.
cards.short_summary: A 493-acre former estate with a network of walking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo says its parks are open daily and admission is free; Wildwood’s page identifies its trail system.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 7 a.m. until dark daily. Metroparks notes that programs and attractions may have separate fees.

cards.title: Walk Swan Creek’s overlooks
cards.subtitle: 4301 Airport Hwy, Toledo
cards.notes: Start from the Airport Highway entrance and follow marked trails toward the creek, scenic overlooks, and swinging bridge.
cards.short_summary: An urban preserve with trails, creek habitat, and wildlife-viewing features.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo lists Swan Creek Preserve as open daily and states Metroparks admission is free.
cards.source_title: Swan Creek Preserve Metropark | Metroparks Toledo
cards.access_notes: Open 7 a.m. until dark every day. Skip reservable facilities if you want to keep the outing free.

cards.title: See public art at Glass City
cards.subtitle: 1505 Front St, Toledo
cards.notes: Walk the riverfront and pause at Beacon Tower, the slag-ladle sculpture, Rain Towers, and Field of Histories.
cards.short_summary: A Maumee River park with documented public-art features.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo states admission is free and identifies public-art features at Glass City Metropark.
cards.access_notes: Most of the park is open 7 a.m. to dark; the Market Hall and Ribbon area has separate posted hours. Paid rentals and food are optional.

cards.title: Do the Middlegrounds trail scavenger hunt
cards.subtitle: 111 Ottawa St, Toledo
cards.notes: Bring a phone or use the posted information cards to follow the one-mile Technology Explorer route from Roundhouse Shelter.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided, geocaching-style activity beside the Maumee River.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo provides a self-guided Technology Explorer at Middlegrounds and states Metroparks admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The route is about one mile round trip and takes roughly 30–45 minutes. Stay on the trail and do not collect natural items.

cards.title: Stroll Toledo Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: 5403 Elmer Dr, Toledo
cards.notes: Pick a garden path, walk at conversation pace, and use the grounds as a relaxed outdoor meetup instead of a ticketed attraction.
cards.short_summary: A named Metroparks garden destination for a no-cost walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Toledo Botanical Garden is a Metroparks Toledo destination, and Metroparks states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Metroparks are open 7 a.m. to dark daily. Do not bring dogs; Metroparks rules exclude dogs from Toledo Botanical Garden.

cards.title: Walk the woods at Secor
cards.subtitle: 10001 Central Ave, Berkey
cards.notes: Choose a marked hiking or all-purpose trail and set an easy turnaround point so the group can explore without needing gear or a reservation.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Metropark for a straightforward woodland walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Secor is a Metroparks Toledo park, and Metroparks states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Metroparks are open 7 a.m. to dark daily. Admission is free, while some programs, attractions, and reservations may have fees.

cards.title: Take a Pearson nature walk
cards.subtitle: 761 S Lallendorf Rd, Oregon
cards.notes: Use the park map to choose a marked route, then pause at the water and woodland areas for a quiet, phone-free group walk.
cards.short_summary: A Metropark day-use destination with walking trails and natural areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Pearson is a Metroparks Toledo park, and Metroparks states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Metroparks are open 7 a.m. to dark daily. Admission is free; avoid reservable facilities and paid programs for a no-cost visit.

cards.title: Rally at Ottawa Park Tennis Courts
cards.subtitle: Ottawa Park, Toledo
cards.notes: Bring your own racquets and balls, reserve a court if needed, and set up a casual doubles rotation for a social hour outdoors.
cards.short_summary: Four city tennis courts designated free for regular play.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Toledo says Ottawa Park’s four tennis courts are always free and may be reserved by residents for regular play.
cards.source_title: Ottawa and Jermain Parks | City of Toledo
cards.access_notes: Bring your own equipment. The city says residents may reserve courts for regular play or events.

cards.title: Ride the Ottawa-Jermain trail
cards.subtitle: Ottawa and Jermain Parks, Toledo
cards.notes: Bring a maintained bike and helmet, stay on the designated 6.4-mile route, and match pace to the least experienced rider in your group.
cards.short_summary: A named city mountain-bike trail with no playing fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Toledo describes the Ottawa-Jermain route as an always-free, 6.4-mile mountain bike trail.
cards.source_title: Ottawa and Jermain Parks | City of Toledo
cards.access_notes: The city lists the trail as always free. Ride within your ability, use appropriate safety gear, and follow posted trail conditions.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments at Mercy College and Toledo Lucas County Public Library, with current access details where published.

cards.title: Mercy College Library
cards.subtitle: Sixth Floor Jefferson, Mercy College of Ohio
cards.notes: Bring coursework to the sixth-floor library for its physical collection, computers, printing, and help from library staff.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with study support, computers, and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College identifies its Library on the sixth floor of Jefferson and lists computers, free black-and-white and color printing, and study use among its highlights.
cards.access_notes: Usually open Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; Mercy says hours may vary and directs visitors to check the library website.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Sixth floor, Mercy College of Ohio
cards.notes: Use the renovated sixth-floor commons when you want to work near the library and classrooms; bring a charged device.
cards.short_summary: A renovated campus commons adjoining Mercy’s new library area.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy says the sixth-floor renovation includes a Learning Commons and that the nearby Health Science Library provides collaborative and private study areas with wired furniture.
cards.source_title: Mercy College of Ohio Unveils New Library with Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony
cards.access_notes: Located within Mercy’s sixth-floor renovation; follow current College building-access guidance.

cards.title: Main Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Toledo Lucas County Public Library Main, 325 Michigan St.
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a focused solo session or a small project group; keep the group to four people or fewer.
cards.short_summary: Reservable small-group rooms at downtown Toledo’s Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library states that its study rooms are free, serve one to four people, and can be reserved by checking availability or calling the library.
cards.source_title: Main Library – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; open Monday–Tuesday 9 a.m.–5:30 p.m., Wednesday–Thursday noon–8:30 p.m., and Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5:30 p.m.

cards.title: Computers and Media Collaboration Rooms
cards.subtitle: First floor, Main Library
cards.notes: Ask at Computers and Media for a collaboration room when a laptop-connected large display would help your group review work.
cards.short_summary: Two display-equipped rooms inside Main Library’s computer area.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Library says its first-floor Computers and Media area has two collaboration rooms with laptop computers and mounted large digital displays.
cards.source_title: Main Library – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: Request use in person at Computers and Media or call 419-259-5200; use during Main Library open hours.

cards.entity_name: Joseph and Judith Conda School Enrichment Room
cards.title: Joseph and Judith Conda School Enrichment Room
cards.subtitle: George K. Saloff Family Children’s Library, Main Library
cards.notes: Choose this named enrichment room for a change of setting, then check with Main Library staff about availability before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A named study room within Main Library’s children’s library.
cards.evidence_claim: Toledo Lucas County Public Library identifies the Joseph and Judith Conda School Enrichment Room as a place where students study.
cards.source_title: The Saloff Children’s Library – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Main Library; confirm room availability with library staff.

cards.title: Small Business and Nonprofit Workspace
cards.subtitle: Parking level, Main Library
cards.notes: Use the named workspace for research or project planning, and consult the Main Library map to locate it on the parking level.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed workspace at downtown Toledo’s Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Toledo Lucas County Public Library’s Main Library map lists a Small Business and Nonprofit Workspace on the parking level.
cards.access_notes: Use during Main Library open hours; ask the help desk about workspace access or availability.

cards.title: West Toledo Quiet Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: West Toledo Branch, 1320 Sylvania Ave.
cards.notes: Head to West Toledo for a quiet room during open hours; rooms are first-come, first-served, so have a backup table in mind.
cards.short_summary: First-come quiet rooms at the West Toledo Branch.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Toledo Branch says quiet study rooms are available first-come, first-served during open hours and that quiet study tables are also available in the main library space.
cards.source_title: West Toledo – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served during open hours: Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8:30 p.m.; Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5:30 p.m.

cards.title: Kent Quiet Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Kent Branch, 3101 Collingwood Blvd.
cards.notes: Try the Kent Branch when you need a quiet room; arrive during open hours and use an in-library table if rooms are occupied.
cards.short_summary: Quiet rooms and study tables at the Kent Branch.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kent Branch states that quiet study rooms are first-come, first-served during open hours and that quiet study tables are often available in its main library space.
cards.source_title: Kent – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served during open hours: Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8:30 p.m.; Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5:30 p.m.

cards.title: Point Place Quiet Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Point Place Branch, 2727 117th St.
cards.notes: Use a first-come quiet room at Point Place for concentrated work, or shift to a quiet study table within the branch.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-room option at the Point Place Branch.
cards.evidence_claim: The Point Place Branch says its quiet study rooms are first-come, first-served during open hours and notes quiet study tables in the main library space.
cards.source_title: Point Place – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served during open hours: Monday–Tuesday 9 a.m.–8:30 p.m.; Wednesday–Friday 9 a.m.–5:30 p.m.

cards.title: King Road Quiet Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: King Road Branch, 3900 King Rd.
cards.notes: Use King Road’s quiet rooms during branch hours for independent work, with quiet tables in the main space as an alternative.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study rooms in the King Road Branch.
cards.evidence_claim: The King Road Branch states that quiet study rooms are available first-come, first-served during open hours and that quiet study tables are often available in the main library space.
cards.source_title: King Road – Toledo Lucas County Public Library
cards.access_notes: First-come, first-served during open hours: Monday–Tuesday noon–8:30 p.m.; Wednesday–Friday 9 a.m.–5:30 p.m.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Mercy College observances and milestone rituals centered on healthcare education, Catholic mission, and campus community.

cards.title: Halloween Howl
cards.subtitle: Mercy College’s annual fall community celebration
cards.notes: Watch the Student Life page for the next Howl, then join the family-friendly activities, costumes, games, and campus decorating when it is announced.
cards.short_summary: A named annual Halloween gathering that brings students, employees, and families together on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College calls Halloween Howl its favorite fall tradition and describes it as an annual community-wide celebration with students, staff, faculty, and families.
cards.access_notes: Details and scheduling are published by the Office of Student Life.

cards.title: De-Stress Yourself Yoga
cards.subtitle: Annual Student Council wellness session
cards.notes: Check Student Life announcements for the annual session and arrive ready for accessible movement, relaxation, and a chance to reset during the term.
cards.short_summary: Student Council’s recurring wellness gathering pairs guided yoga with relaxation and community connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College’s Student Life page identifies De-Stress Yourself Yoga as an annual Student Council event for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: The college says the session is designed for all skill levels and is led by a trained professional.

cards.title: New Student Orientation
cards.subtitle: Mercy College’s annual welcome for new students
cards.notes: Use orientation to meet faculty and staff, take the campus tour, and begin connecting with classmates before classes settle into their routine.
cards.short_summary: A recurring starting-point ritual where new Mercy students are welcomed into the college community.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College says the Office of Student Life welcomes hundreds of students and parents to New Student Orientation each year.
cards.access_notes: Orientation dates are listed on Mercy College’s events calendar.

cards.title: Weekly Prayer Service
cards.subtitle: Recurring Mercy College faith observance
cards.notes: Consult the college events calendar for the next prayer service and attend if a short, scheduled campus observance fits your day.
cards.short_summary: A regular campus prayer practice reflecting the college’s Catholic identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College’s current events calendar lists “Mercy College of Ohio - Weekly Prayer Service” as a recurring event.
cards.access_notes: The events calendar supplies the current date, time, and event details.

cards.title: PA Program White Coat Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Physician Assistant program milestone
cards.notes: If you are in the PA program, confirm ceremony information with the program and plan around the published date, time, and Toledo listing.
cards.short_summary: A formal white-coat milestone marking a stage in Mercy’s Physician Assistant program.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College’s events calendar lists a “PA Program-White Coat Ceremony - Toledo.”
cards.access_notes: The calendar’s event listing provides the current scheduling information.

cards.title: Nursing Pinning Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Nursing graduates’ Mercy College rite of passage
cards.notes: Graduating nursing students should follow their program’s instructions and the graduation page for the applicable pinning ceremony location and arrival details.
cards.short_summary: A program-specific nursing graduation ritual with a distinct professional symbol at its center.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College describes its nursing pin as a “rite of passage and tradition” into a caring profession, and its graduation page lists nursing pinning ceremonies.
cards.source_title: Mercy College of Ohio Virtual Pinning Ceremony | Mercy College
cards.access_notes: Current nursing pinning logistics are posted on the graduation and commencement page.

cards.title: The Nursing Pin Presentation
cards.subtitle: The central object ritual of Mercy nursing pinning
cards.notes: For a visual record of the ritual, review Mercy’s pinning coverage and graduation materials; the nursing pin is the ceremony’s documented professional symbol.
cards.short_summary: Mercy’s nursing pin functions as the tangible emblem used to mark entry into the profession.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College states that the nursing pin represents a rite of passage and tradition into a profession committed to caring.
cards.source_title: Mercy College of Ohio Virtual Pinning Ceremony | Mercy College
cards.access_notes: This is part of the nursing pinning ceremony for eligible graduates.

cards.title: Blessing of Hands
cards.subtitle: Nursing pinning’s care-centered observance
cards.notes: Treat this as a ceremony element for nursing graduates and invited attendees; confirm the current program with the nursing division before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A documented blessing incorporated into Mercy’s nursing-graduate pinning ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College’s nursing pinning event description says the ceremony included the Blessing of Hands alongside song, speeches, and nursing-pin awards.
cards.source_title: Spring 2020 Pinning Ceremony Nursing Graduates | Mercy College
cards.access_notes: The cited event documents this ceremony practice; consult current program communications for participation details.

cards.title: Mercy College Commencement
cards.subtitle: College-wide graduation ceremony
cards.notes: Graduation candidates should use the Student Records page for the current ceremony schedule, RSVP process, regalia deadline, and venue instructions.
cards.short_summary: Mercy’s formal college-wide celebration for graduates across nursing and allied-health programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College publishes commencement ceremonies and graduation information for its degree and certificate candidates.
cards.access_notes: The page provides current commencement details and links to recordings of prior ceremonies.

cards.title: Misericordia et Cura Award
cards.subtitle: Mercy College’s highest honor at commencement
cards.notes: Look for the award presentation in commencement coverage and use it as a lens for the college motto: compassion and care in the healing ministry.
cards.short_summary: A commencement-honors ritual recognizing service aligned with Mercy College’s core motto.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College identifies the Misericordia et Cura Award as its highest honor and says it recognizes lives that embody compassion and care.
cards.access_notes: The award was presented during Mercy College’s spring commencement ceremony described in the cited report.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Mercy College of Ohio, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence that starts with campus resources and opens into Toledo art and riverfront space.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the Library
cards.subtitle: Mercy College of Ohio • Toledo campus
cards.notes: Start by locating a dependable study and printing stop. Walk through the library, note its layout, and save the services page for later coursework.
cards.short_summary: A practical first campus stop for studying, printing, and getting oriented.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College describes its library as a place to study, print, or hang out.
cards.access_notes: Campus resource; confirm building access and service availability with Mercy College.

cards.title: Take a movement break at the Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the main Jefferson entrance
cards.notes: Follow the posted signs to see the fitness room and locker-room location. Bring any required waiver or access materials before planning a workout.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus option for a brief, equipment-based reset.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fitness Center has treadmills, exercise bikes, free weights, weight machines, mats, and locker rooms with showers.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of the main Jefferson entrance; follow posted signs and complete any required waiver.

cards.title: Save the Food Pantry resource
cards.subtitle: Mercy College of Ohio • Toledo campus
cards.notes: If you need groceries or household support, save this page early. Eligible campus community members may visit without an appointment while the college is open.
cards.short_summary: A campus support resource to keep on hand from day one.
cards.evidence_claim: The Food Pantry is available to Mercy College students, faculty, and staff; no appointment is required.
cards.access_notes: Available to students, faculty, and staff anytime the college is open; the College requests that inquiries come from a Mercy email address.

cards.title: Find a way to participate through Student Council
cards.subtitle: Mercy College of Ohio student life
cards.notes: Read the current Student Council page and send a question to Student Life if you want to learn about organizations, activities, or ways to participate.
cards.short_summary: A documented entry point to student organizations and campus involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College says all students, including Toledo-campus and online students, are welcome to participate in Student Council.
cards.access_notes: Contact studentgovernment@mercycollege.edu or studentlife@mercycollege.edu for information about organizations and involvement.

cards.entity_name: Mercy College Campus Ministry and Service Learning
cards.title: Explore service and ministry options
cards.subtitle: Mercy College of Ohio student affairs
cards.notes: Look through the Campus Ministry and Service Learning information, then choose a future opportunity that fits your schedule rather than overfilling your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus-supported route toward worship, service learning, and volunteering.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercy College lists Campus Ministry and Service Learning among its student-affairs resources.
cards.source_title: Student Affairs and Resources | Mercy College
cards.access_notes: Consult Mercy College Student Affairs for current opportunities and participation details.

cards.title: Make an art-museum afternoon of it
cards.subtitle: 2445 Monroe Street • Toledo
cards.notes: Set aside time to walk the main museum at your own pace. Check the visit page before leaving for current visitor guidance and exhibition details.
cards.short_summary: A free general-admission museum visit close to Mercy College’s Toledo campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Toledo Museum of Art states that general admission is free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Toledo Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Visit during the museum's regular public hours; review the visit page for current details.

cards.entity_name: Toledo Museum of Art Glass Pavilion
cards.title: Continue to the Glass Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Toledo Museum of Art campus • 2445 Monroe Street
cards.notes: Add the Glass Pavilion as a separate stop after the main museum. Use the museum’s events and visit information to check what is open that day.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated glass-collection and working-studio setting on the museum campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum identifies the Glass Pavilion as the location for its public glassblowing demonstrations.
cards.source_title: Glassblowing Demonstrations | Toledo Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Check the museum before travel, as Pavilion closures or special events can affect access.

cards.title: Watch the 2 p.m. glassblowing demonstration
cards.subtitle: Glass Pavilion Hot Shop • Toledo Museum of Art
cards.notes: Plan your museum route around the 2 p.m. demonstration, then arrive early enough to find the Hot Shop. Check for cancellations before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A daily public look at glassmaking by the museum’s glass artists.
cards.evidence_claim: The Toledo Museum of Art offers free fine-art glassblowing demonstrations every day at 2 p.m. in the Glass Pavilion.
cards.source_title: Glassblowing Demonstrations | Toledo Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Scheduled daily at 2 p.m.; annual maintenance, special events, or closures can affect the schedule.

cards.title: Take a riverside walk at Middlegrounds
cards.subtitle: 111 Ottawa Street • Toledo
cards.notes: Finish the daytime outing with the walk/bike path and Maumee River views. Stay on marked paths, dress for conditions, and leave before dark.
cards.short_summary: A downtown riverfront park with a documented walk/bike path.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlegrounds Metropark has a 1.5-mile walk/bike path and a half-mile of Maumee River frontage.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 7 a.m. until dark. Metroparks Toledo states that park admission is free, though programs and attractions may charge fees.

cards.title: Turn the river walk into a scavenger hunt
cards.subtitle: Middlegrounds Metropark • 111 Ottawa Street
cards.notes: Load the listed GPS points or make it a no-device scavenger hunt. Keep to the trail and leave plants and other natural items where you find them.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided, geocaching-style activity along the Middlegrounds path.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo describes the Technology Explorer as a geocaching-style adventure whose information cards are visible from the trail.
cards.source_title: Metroparks Technology Explorer: Middlegrounds Metropark | Metroparks Toledo
cards.access_notes: The course begins at the Roundhouse Shelter and is described as about one mile round trip; stay on trail and do not collect or damage nature items.
